title: upgrade-attn-flashattnv2-rope-fused-kv-batching-scheduling
author: Ethan Brooks
commits: feat(attention): integrate FlashAttentionV2 kernels with fused rotary/rope ops
perf(kv): harmonize KV cache layout for fused kernels and continuous batching
fix(scheduler): prefer small-batch low-latency path for real-time routes
test: add microbench harness and unit tests for fused attention paths
chore: feature-flag for flashattnv2 rollout and canary config
description:
Context: We're seeing headroom on throughput and latency for mid- to long-context workloads by moving to the FlashAttentionV2 kernels and fusing rotary/rope computation into the attention kernel. This PR upgrades the runtime attention implementation to use FlashAttentionV2 where available and introduces a fused rotary/rope path + KV-cache layout changes to avoid extra copies when using continuous batching.

What this changes (high level):
- Integrates FlashAttentionV2 kernels with an opt-in feature flag (runtime.feature_flags.flashattnv2).
- Implements fused rotary/rope math inside the attention kernel to reduce elementwise ops and memory traffic.
- Reworks the KV cache layout and accessors so fused kernels can read/write KV with zero-copy when running continuous batching.
- Scheduler heuristics updated to prefer the low-latency small-batch path for real-time routes and fall back to high-throughput path for large queued batches.
- Adds microbench harness + unit tests and a canary rollout plan under the dedicate cluster autoscaler (release gating).

Motivation: The current FlashAttentionV1 + separate rotary implementation creates memory-bound workloads for long-context generation and costs an additional kernel launch per layer. Fusing the rotary/rope work into the attention kernel reduces memory traffic and kernel launch overheads. Combined with KV layout changes this reduces per-token latency and increases GPU utilization with continuous batching.

Benchmarks: (microbench on A100-80GB, batch sizes 1/4/16, seq len 2048)
- Throughput +18% at batch 16 (same memory budget)
- P50 latency -12% for batch=1, seq=2048
- Peak CUDA memory usage -25% for batch 4 with prefetched KVs
- End-to-end inference p90 for live canary routes improved ~9% (preliminary)

Backward compatibility and rollout:
- Feature-flagged (off by default for older clusters).
- Automatically falls back to legacy kernels if FlashAttentionV2 not available or if model config requests separate rotary path.
- Canary rollout steps included in docs/notes/upgrade-flashattnv2.md.

Checklist:
- [x] kernel integration and fused rotary math
- [x] KV layout change and accessors
- [x] scheduler heuristic updates and config knobs
- [x] unit + perf tests
- [x] docs + canary plan

Ethan Brooks: Good catch - added tests/perf/bench_flashattn_v2.py and a unit that reproduces the odd-length case; fixed an off-by-one in the masking branch.
Marcus Li: Please ensure the KV layout change is strictly versioned so existing cached blobs are still readable by older runtimes.
Ethan Brooks: KV cache now includes a version header and compatibility shim; added migration in kv_cache_layout.h.
release_notes: Upgrade: FlashAttentionV2 + fused rotary/rope ops; KV cache layout optimized for fused kernels; scheduler heuristics improved for low-latency routes. See docs/notes/upgrade-flashattnv2.md for rollout steps and canary instructions.
